answer.rationale: P99 write latency is elevated 5x during settlement peak. The security patch cannot be rolled back per compliance. Routing read queries to replicas (memory_b5) successfully reduced primary load and recovered write latency the same day without touching the release. This preserves the mandatory security patch while immediately relieving write-path pressure. Regional failover (memory_b2) is retained as contingency if primary degradation worsens, but routing reads first is lower-risk and directly addresses the bottleneck. Adding capacity takes time we don't have; circuit breakers don't resolve the underlying latency. This intervention targets the load distribution without reverting protected code.
